name: Camera extensions and hardware camera controls
plain: Uses vendor camera modes (night, HDR, bokeh) and hardware buttons from inside an app.
meaning: Lets third-party apps match the stock camera's processing. The photos still need camera permission; the extras mainly affect image quality, not access.

android.prompt_ui: Camera prompt: While using the app, Only this time, Don't allow
android.api_surface: CameraX ExtensionsManager, Camera2 CameraExtensionSession (API 31), Android 16 Camera2 hybrid auto exposure and Night Mode indicator
android.note: Extensions: Night, HDR, Bokeh, Face Retouch, Auto; availability per OEM.

ios.permission: NSCameraUsageDescription; Camera Control via AVCaptureSession; LockedCameraCapture extension entitlement
ios.api_surface: AVCaptureSession, AVCaptureSystemZoomSlider and AVCaptureSlider (Camera Control, iOS 18), LockedCameraCapture, AVCaptureDeviceRotationCoordinator
ios.note: iOS 18 adds Camera Control (iPhone 16) hooks and a lock screen camera extension that runs with a limited sandbox.

limits.headline: Can use phone camera modes such as night and HDR, after you allow the camera
limits.user_action: You tap Allow for the camera, then choose a mode such as Night
can: Use Night, HDR, Bokeh, Face Retouch or Auto modes where the phone supports them (Android 10)
Use Camera Control on iPhone 16 and a lock screen camera extension (iOS 18)
Match the stock camera's photo quality
cannot: Use the camera without the Allow prompt
Use every mode on every phone; it depends on the maker
Get extra access to your photos from these modes
limits.reach_label: While the camera is in use
limits.differs: Android lists modes per phone maker. iOS 18 adds Camera Control on iPhone 16.

story.what_it_is: Lets third party camera apps use the phone's night, HDR and portrait modes.

marketing.name: CameraX Extensions API
marketing.pitch: Use device vendors' camera modes like night, HDR and bokeh in your app.

story.for_you: Photos in your favorite camera or social app can look as good as the stock camera, with night mode and portrait blur.
story.for_makers: Matching the stock camera's processing makes third party apps feel premium. Camera permission is still needed, and the extras mainly improve image quality, not access.

use_cases.example: You take a night photo in Instagram and it looks bright and sharp.
A pro camera app uses the phone's portrait blur on a headshot.
A video call app uses HDR to fix a dark room.
A marketplace app shows clearer item photos at night.
A deposit app uses better focus to read a check.
An AR game gets a cleaner image under low light.

story.android_note: CameraX Extensions work on supported Android phones from several makers.
story.ios_note: iOS apps use AVFoundation with similar camera controls on newer iPhones.

technical_bounds: Camera indicator dot and permission still apply

history.change: Camera Control and lock screen camera extensions
